messages.subject: Update, Package reorganization & refactoring
messages.subject_clean: Update, Package reorganization & refactoring
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm planning some package reorganization over the next week or so to address some licensing issues, clarify the structure of the code, and integrate the new interpreter/jitting compiler.
I'm not sure to what extent folks have outstanding commits, or are referencing the API in other projects, so I thought I would give a heads up.

First,
I've acquired the renjin.org <http://renjin.org> domain, so I will be moving all code into the org.renjin package to better conform with java coding conventions.

Here is the basic outline:

module org.renjin:renjin-data
License: LGPL
Classes:  vectors and other data structures, and data reader/writer
(mostly former r.lang),  e.g.:

org.renjin.data.SEXP
org.renjin.data.Vector
org.renjin.data.DoubleVector
org.renjin.data.Environment
etc

module org.renjin:renjin-math
License: GPL
Includes any math routines that could be
independently useful to a Java developer
org.renjin.math.xx

module org.renjin:renjin-interpreter
License: GPL
org.renjin.interpreter
org.renjin.interpreter
org.renjin.compiler
org.renjin.primitives
org.renjin.base

The idea being that between the javax.scripting and org.renjin.data classes, java programmers can depend on renjin without directly referencing GPL'd APIs. (I'm still a bit foggy as to the consequences of this-- I would like to license renjin as liberally as possible but renjin is absolutely derivative of the GPL'd R and I want to honor that)

Best,

Alex

  #summary Plan of Attack
  #sidebar SideBar

-** IN PROGRESS **
-
-= Introduction =
-
-This is the general _plan de campagne_ for Renjin, a project that is in
equal parts a port and a rewrite of the [http://www.r-project.org R
project]'s interpreter of the R Language for Statistical Computing.
-
-The R language and its sole interpreter to date have evolved together over
a period of decades, so any attempt to implement a new interpreter of the R
language without reference (and deference!) to its abrahamic implementation
would be unlikely to succeed. Renjin's core borrows heavily from the
original C code, indeed, many portions remain literal translations from C
to Java.
-
-At the same time, Renjin is attempt to modernize the internals of the
interpreter and to profit from the strengths of the JVM in areas such as
garbage collection, unicode handling and I/O. The latent object-oriented
character of the original SEXP has been expanded to a full-fledged class
hierarchy, and most primitive functions have been written from scratch
based documentation and experimentation with the R repl.
-
-= Front End =
-
-The front end of the interpreter/compiler parses R language programs into
an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST).
-
-Renjin's
[http://code.google.com/p/renjin/source/browse/trunk/core/src/main/java/r/parser/RLexer.java
lexer] is ported directly from the C.
-
-Renjin's parser is built from the original
[http://www.google.com/codesearch#ph23m5MVwzs/trunk/R-2.10.1-patched/src/main/gram.y&q=package:r4jvm%20file:gram.y&l=1
gram.y] using the java extension of the [http://www.gnu.org/software/bison/
Bison parser generator]
-
-
-= Strings and Character Encodings =
-
-Since Renjin implements R character vectors with Java strings, all
character vectors are encoded in UTF-8.
-
-= Base Library =
-
-R's 'base' package (as well as other 'recommended' packages) are divided
into portions written in the R-language and 'primitives' written in
C/Fortran/Java.
-
-Renjin's uses the R Project's R-language base library without
modification. This help ensures compatibility with the original interpreter
and will facilitate renjin's evolution alongside the C-based interpreter.
-
-While the native portion of R's base library is huge -- nearly 700
functions coded in C -- much of the heavy lifting, from linear algebra to
regexs, can be delegating to existing [ThirdParty libraries for the JVM].
-
-
+
+= Plan of Attack 2012 =
+
+Renjin has come a long way over the last year. What started as an idle
experiment has progressed substantially over the last year: the interpreter
has now been used to run real-world R code in real-world situations
(specifically the aspects and survey packages) and performance rivals that
of the original interpreter written in C.
+
+R on the JVM offers many advantages:
+  * Scalable web services written in R (running on Google AppEngine for
example)
+  * Seamless integration with big data frameworks like Hadoop
+  * Access for R-programmers to best-of-breed JVM libraries outside of the
statistical domain, such as database access, geographic information
information systems, web servers, etc.
+
+But we're not quite there yet! The following document outlines what is
required to advance Renjin to a 1.0 release in 2012 -- and each of these
major sections could use an owner!
+
+== Core functionality ==
+
+About 60% of the nearly 700 primitive functions are implemented. The
following are major groups of functions that require substantial investment
to start and/or complete:
+
+  * Complex numbers
+  * File manipulations (file.xxx)
+  * S4 objects
+  * Graphics engine (started, but not complete)
+  * operations on connections (readLines, writeLines, scan, etc)
+  * migrate to R2.14 base libraries (2.10 is currently being used)
+
+== Tooling / JVM Interop ==
+  * Complete javax.scripting interface
+  * Classfile generator in order to implement JVM interfaces/classes with
R code (relevant for Hadoop, for example)
+  * Maven plugin to simplify packaging R libraries as jars
+
+== Key Libraries ==
+
+  * Hadoop integration - Jiessie
+  * JDBC library for R
+
+== IDE ==
+  * Integrate Renjin into StatET
+
+== Performance ==
+  * JIT optimizing compiler - Alex
+  * Implement out-of-memory alternatives for Vector interfaces

+= Interpreter =
+
+There are two interpreters under development: the so-called Mark I
interpreter (working) and the Mark II jitting interpreter.
+
+== Mark I ==
+
+The Mark I is currently used by Renjin and is implemented in the same
fashion as R.2X. The evaluator simply descends the AST recursively
evaluating symbols, function calls, and promises as they are encountered.

the moment.

intermediate representation that is more efficent to execute, and will
eventually feature type inference and narrowing (from vectors to scalars)
and just-in-time compilation to byte code.

Hi Jiessie,

Hope you don't mind, I'm copying the contributors group on this because I think there is a wider interest.

The JRMapReduceCooker is looking good! To make it easy to reuse, perhaps we could split it into two maven projects -- the first jar with R and java support routines, and the second a maven plugin that handles the packaging of the user's mapper/reducer into a jar for deployment to hadoop.

I think ultimately we need a generic util in renjin core that generates a class file stub which implements an interface or abstract class by calling out to R scripts. It shouldn't be so hard to do with libasm, may be you could give a try?

Have you been able to work around national restrictions and access the google repo? Again, if you're still having problems we can convert the repo to git and then create a mirror on github where you can commit.

Best,

Alex

+= Bean classes =
+
+For Java classes with accessor methods that conform to the getXX(),
setXX()/isXX() bean convention, Renjin provides some special sauce to make
access from R more natural.
+
+Given the java bean:
+
+{{{
+class Customer {
+  String name;
+  int age;
+
+  String getName() { return name; }
+  void setName(String name) { this.name <http://this.name> = name; }
+
+  int getAge() { return age; }
+  void setAge(int age) { this.age = age; }
+}
+}}}
+
+You can construct a new instance of the Customer class and provide initial
values with named arguments to the constructor:
+
+{{{
+import(com.acme.Customer)
+
+bob <- Customer$new(name='Bob', age=36)
+carol <- Customer$new(name='Carole', age=41)
+}}}
+
+Java bean properties must be accessed as variables rather than through
method calls:
+
+{{{
+   bob$name <- "Bob II"
+   cat(c("Name: ", bob$name, "; Age: ", bob$age))
+}}}
+

Hi Ido,

That's correct; C and Fortran code in such packages would need to be
either:
1. Ported to pure R
2. Ported to java
3. Compiled to JVM byte code via c2j or f2j or other similar project

necessary)

These contraints mean that Renjin will not immediately be useful to
all current users; indeed the project is very much a work in progress;
using Renjin today means being will to get under the hood and tinker!

pure R implementations for their packages, but this probably won't be
